messages.author: 21a8a078d448ab4f
messages.subject: Overlapped transects
parts:
Hi all,
I have a question about survey designs. I designed a survey laying
transects 3 km apart each other. Once I finished the survey I discovered
with a GIS software that in fact some transects were separated a bit less

than the 3 km predefined distance, so areas searched (outer distances)
overlapped 10-20%. Some of these transects were searched within the same

day while others were separated in time (2-3 days). Do I have to consider
those transects overlapped as one sampling unit (summing effort and
observations in one transect?
Thanks in advance
Alejandro

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: Re: Overlapped transects
parts:
Alejandro, while this violates the independence assumption, the implication=
s of such overlap are minor. Variance estimates are robust to this effect.=
For an illustration of this for point transect sampling, see=20
Buckland, S.T. 2006. Point transect surveys for songbirds: robust methodo=
logies. The Auk 123, 345-357.
I'll send you a copy of this off-list.

Steve Buckland
